packages.label: שֵׁם ה' וְהַחִיּוּת
packages.label_en: The Divine Name and the Life-Force
packages.reason: These four nodes all express the same essential reality: the Divine Name as the living essence of all existence. 'The Name is the life-force' (הַשֵּׁם הוּא הַחִיּוּת) and 'Shabbat is the Name of the Holy One' (שַׁבָּת שְׁמָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא) — Name, life-force, and Shabbat are all parallel expressions of the same divine presence. Shabbat was commanded immediately after Yom Kippur precisely because after Yom Kippur the Name of God is revealed, and Shabbat itself IS that Name. The two raw components {שם, חיות} and {שבת, שמא דקדשא בריך הוא} are merged because their proof texts are drawn from the same passage and orbit the identical theological claim: the Name of God = life.

merge_notes.reason: The raw component {שבת, שמא דקדשא בריך הוא} is merged with {שם, חיות} because both components express the identical claim: the Divine Name = the living essence of reality. The proof text for both edges states that the Name is the life-force (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָה הוּא שְׁמוֹ) and that Shabbat is the Name of God (שַׁבָּת שְׁמָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא). Shabbat, the Name, and life-force are three faces of the same divine presence — not cause-and-effect, but parallel aspects of one reality.

packages.label: הַצַּדִּיק וְיְסוֹד הַפָּשׁוּט
packages.label_en: The Tzaddik and the Simple Foundation
packages.reason: The Tzaddik is explicitly identified as the 'Simple Foundation' (יְסוֹד הַפָּשׁוּט) — the single root from which the four elemental forces of all existence flow. These two nodes are two names for the same cosmic reality: the unitary source beneath all multiplicity. The verse 'צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם' (Proverbs 10) identifies the Tzaddik as the foundation of the world, and the teaching identifies this as the Simple Foundation — the unified root that precedes the split into four rivers/elements. This is the positive pole of the Torah: the Tzaddik as the world's sustaining root.

packages.label: עֳנָשִׁים וּמִיתָה
packages.reason: These two nodes are parallel expressions of the same negative reality: punishment at any level is a form of death, because it uproots a person from the root of their life-force. The Gemara (Avodah Zarah 5a) interprets 'they died' as 'they became poor' — confirming that even loss of wealth or status constitutes a bechina of death. Since the Name/life-force is the positive pole (Package 1), punishment/death is its direct negative mirror: the domain where the life-connection is severed. This is the evil mirror of Package 1: just as the Name = life, punishment = death (severance from the Name).
